1.1: And it came to be after the death of Sha’ul, when Dawiḏ had returned from smiting the Amalĕqites, that Dawiḏ remained two days in Tsiqlaḡ.
1.2: And it came to be on the third day, that see, a man came out of the camp from Sha’ul with his garments torn and dust on his head. And it came to be, when he came to Dawiḏ, that he fell to the ground and did obeisance.
1.3: And Dawiḏ said to him, “From where do you come?” And he said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Yisra’ĕl.”
1.4: And Dawiḏ said to him, “What was the matter? Please inform me.” And he said, “The people have fled from the battle, and also many of the people have fallen and are dead, and Sha’ul and Yahonathan his son are dead too.”
1.5: And Dawiḏ said to the young man who informed him, “How do you know that Sha’ul and Yahonathan his son are dead?”
1.6: And the young man who informed him said, “By chance I was on Mount Gilboa and saw Sha’ul leaning on his spear. And see, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
1.7: “And when he looked behind him, he saw me and called to me, and I answered, ‘Here I am.’
1.8: “And he said to me, ‘Who are you?’ So I answered him, ‘I am an Amalĕqite.’
1.9: “And he said to me, ‘Please stand over me and put me to death, for agony has seized me, but my life is still in me.’
1.10: “So I stood beside him and put him to death, for I knew he would not live after he had fallen. And I took the diadem that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them here to my master.”
1.11: And Dawiḏ took hold of his own garments and tore them, and also all the men who were with him.
1.12: And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Sha’ul and for Yahonathan his son, and for the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and for the house of Yisra’ĕl, because they had fallen by the sword.
1.13: Then Dawiḏ asked the young man who informed him, “Where are you from?” And he answered, “I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalĕqite.”
1.14: And Dawiḏ said to him, “How was it you were not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
1.15: And Dawiḏ called one of the young men and said, “Draw near and fall on him!” And he smote him so that he died.
1.16: And Dawiḏ said to him, “Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth has witnessed against you, saying, ‘I myself have put to death the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”
1.17: Then Dawiḏ lamented with this lamentation over Sha’ul and over Yahonathan his son,
1.18: and he ordered “The Bow” to be taught to the children of Yahuḏah. See, it is written in the Book of Yashar:
1.19:
“The splendor of Yisra’ĕl 
Is slain on your high places! 
How the mighty have fallen!
1.20:
“Declare it not in Gath, 
Proclaim it not in the streets of Ashqelon, 
Lest the daughters of the Pelishtites rejoice, 
Lest the daughters of the  uncircumcised exult.
1.21:
“Mountains of Gilboa!
No dew or rain be upon you, 
Nor fields of offerings. 
For there the shield of the mighty lay rejected, 
The shield of Sha’ul, not anointed with	oil.
1.22:
“From the blood of the slain, 
From the fat of the mighty, 
The bow of Yahonathan did not turn back, 
And the sword of Sha’ul did not return empty.
1.23:
“Sha’ul and Yahonathan were beloved 
And pleasant in their lives, 
And in their death they were not parted. 
They were swifter than eagles, 
They were stronger than lions.
1.25:
“How the mighty have fallen 
In the midst of the battle! 
Yahonathan was slain in your high places.
1.26:
“I am distressed for you, my brother Yahonathan. 
You have been very pleasant to me. 
Your love to me was wondrous, 
Surpassing the love of women.
1.27:
“How the mighty have fallen, 
And the weapons of battle perish!”

10.1: And after this it came to be that the meleḵ of the children of Ammon died, and Ḥanun his son reigned in his place.
10.2: And Dawiḏ said, “Let me show kindness to Ḥanun son of Naḥash, as his father showed kindness to me.” So Dawiḏ sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And when Dawiḏ’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon,
10.3: the chiefs of the children of Ammon said to Ḥanun their master, “Is Dawiḏ esteeming your father in your eyes in that he has sent comforters to you? Has Dawiḏ not rather sent his servants to you to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?”
10.4: So Ḥanun took Dawiḏ’s servants and shaved off half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.
10.5: And they informed Dawiḏ, and he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the meleḵ said, “Wait at Yeriḥo until your beards have grown, and then return.”
10.6: And when the children of Ammon saw that they had become a stench to Dawiḏ, the children of Ammon sent and hired Arameans of Bĕyth Reḥoḇ and Arameans of Tsoḇa, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the meleḵ of Ma’aḵah, one thousand men, and men of Toḇ, twelve thousand men.
10.7: And Dawiḏ heard, and sent Yo’aḇ and the entire army, the mighty men.
10.8: And the children of Ammon came out and put themselves in battle array at the entrance of the gate. And the Arameans of Tsoḇa, and Reḥoḇ, and men of Toḇ, and Ma’aḵah were by themselves in the field.
10.9: And Yo’aḇ saw that the battle line was against him before and behind, and he chose out of all the chosen men of Yisra’ĕl and put them in battle array against the Arameans.
10.10: And the rest of the people he gave under the hand of Aḇishai his brother, and he put them in battle array against the children of Ammon.
10.11: And he said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I shall come and help you.
10.12: “Be strong, and let us show strength for our people and for the cities of our Elohim, and let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 do what is good in His eyes.”
10.13: And Yo’aḇ drew near, and the people with him, to battle against Aram, and they fled before him.
10.14: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they also fled before Aḇishai, and went into the city. And Yo’aḇ returned from the children of Ammon and came to Yerushalayim.
10.15: And Aram saw that they were smitten before Yisra’ĕl, and they gathered together,
10.16: and Haḏaḏezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Ḥĕlam. And Shoḇaḵ the commander of the army of Haḏaḏezer went before them.
10.17: And it was reported to Dawiḏ, and he gathered all Yisra’ĕl, and passed over the Yardĕn, and came to Ḥĕlam. And Aram put themselves in battle array against Dawiḏ and they fought with him.
10.18: And Aram fled before Yisra’ĕl, and Dawiḏ slew seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand horsemen of Aram, and he smote Shoḇaḵ, commander of their army, who died there.
10.19: And all the melaḵim, the servants of Haḏaḏezer, saw that they were smitten by Yisra’ĕl, and made peace with Yisra’ĕl, and served them. And the Arameans were afraid to help the children of Ammon any more.

11.1: And it came to be at the turn of the year, at the time melaḵim go out, that Dawiḏ sent Yo’aḇ and his servants with him, and all Yisra’ĕl, and they destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But Dawiḏ remained at Yerushalayim.
11.2: And it came to be, at evening time, that Dawiḏ rose up from his bed and walked about on the roof of the meleḵ’s house. And from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very good to look at.
11.3: And Dawiḏ sent and asked about the woman, and one said, “Is this not Bathsheḇa, the daughter of Eliyam, the wife of Uriyah the Ḥittite?”
11.4: And Dawiḏ sent messengers, to fetch her. And she came to him, and he lay with her - for she was cleansing herself from her uncleanness - and she returned to her house.
11.5: And the woman conceived, and sent and informed Dawiḏ, and said, “I am pregnant.”
11.6: Then Dawiḏ sent to Yo’aḇ, “Send Uriyah the Ḥittite to me.” And Yo’aḇ sent Uriyah to Dawiḏ.
11.7: And Uriyah came to him, and Dawiḏ asked how Yo’aḇ was doing, and how the people were doing, and how the fighting was going.
11.8: And Dawiḏ said to Uriyah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” And Uriyah went out from the meleḵ’s house, and a gift from the meleḵ followed him.
11.9: But Uriyah lay down at the door of the meleḵ’s house with all the servants of his master, and did not go down to his house.
11.10: And they informed Dawiḏ, saying, “Uriyah did not go down to his house,” So Dawiḏ said to Uriyah, “Did you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?”
11.11: And Uriyah said to Dawiḏ, “The ark and Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah are dwelling in booths, and my master Yo’aḇ and the servants of my master are encamped in the open fields. And I, should I go to my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your being lives, let me not do this.”
11.12: And Dawiḏ said to Uriyah, “Remain here today also, and tomorrow I let you go.” So Uriyah remained in Yerushalayim, that day and the next.
11.13: And Dawiḏ called him, and he ate and drank before him, and he made him drunk. And at evening he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his master, but he did not go down to his house.
11.14: And it came to be in the morning that Dawiḏ wrote a letter to Yo’aḇ and sent it by the hand of Uriyah.
11.15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, “Put Uriyah in the front of the heaviest battle, and you shall turn away from him, and he shall be smitten and shall die.”
11.16: And it came to be, as Yo’aḇ watched the city, that he appointed Uriyah to the place where he knew there were brave men.
11.17: And the men of the city came out and fought with Yo’aḇ. And some of the people of the servants of Dawiḏ fell. And Uriyah the Ḥittite also died.
11.18: And Yo’aḇ sent and reported to Dawiḏ all the events of the battle,
11.19: and commanded the messenger, saying, “When you have finished reporting all the events of the battle to the meleḵ,
11.20: then it shall be, if the meleḵ’s wrath rises and he says to you, ‘Why did you go so near to the city when you fought? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?
11.21: ‘Who smote Aḇimeleḵ the son of Yerubbesheth? Was it not a woman who threw an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thĕḇĕts? Why did you go near the wall?’ Then you shall say, ‘Your servant Uriyah the Ḥittite is also dead.’ ”
11.22: And the messenger went, and came and reported to Dawiḏ all with which Yo’aḇ had sent him.
11.23: And the messenger said to Dawiḏ, “The men have been mighty against us and came out to us in the field, but we drove them back as far as the entrance of the gate.
11.24: “And the archers shot from the wall at your servants. And some of the meleḵ’s servants are dead, and your servant Uriyah the Ḥittite is also dead.”
11.25: And Dawiḏ said to the messenger, “Say to Yo’aḇ, ‘Do not let this matter be evil in your eyes, for the sword devours one as well as another. Strengthen your attack against the city, and overthrow it.’ And encourage him.”
11.26: And the wife of Uriyah heard that Uriyah her husband was dead, and she lamented for her husband.
11.27: And when her mourning was over, Dawiḏ sent and brought her to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the deed that Dawiḏ had done was evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

12.1: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent Nathan to Dawiḏ. And he came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor.
12.2: “The rich one had flocks and herds, very many.
12.3: “But the poor one had only one little ewe lamb which he had bought and kept alive. And it grew up with him and with his children together. It ate of his own food and drank from his own cup and lay in his bosom. And it was like a daughter to him.
12.4: “And a traveler came to the rich man, who refused to take from his own flock and from his own herd to prepare one for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”
12.5: And the wrath of Dawiḏ burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, the man who has done this is a son of death!
12.6: “Also, he has to repay fourfold for the lamb, because he did this deed and because he had no compassion.”
12.7: Then Nathan said to Dawiḏ, “You are the man! Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘I anointed you meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl, and I delivered you from the hand of Sha’ul.
12.8: ‘And I gave you your master’s house and your master’s wives into your bosom, and gave you the house of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah. And if that were not enough, I also would have given you much more!
12.9: ‘Why have you despised the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to do evil in His eyes? You have killed Uriyah the Ḥittite with the sword, and his wife you took to be your wife, and you have killed him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
12.10: ‘And now, the sword does not turn aside from your house, because you have despised Me, and have taken the wife of Uriyah the Ḥittite to be your wife.’
12.11: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I am raising up evil against you, from your own house, and shall take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
12.12: ‘For you did it in secret, but I shall do this deed before all Yisra’ĕl, and before the sun.’ ”
12.13: And Dawiḏ said to Nathan, “I have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And Nathan said to Dawiḏ, “Also, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has put away your sin, you shall not die.
12.14: “However, because by this deed you have greatly scorned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the child also who is born to you shall certainly die.”
12.15: And Nathan went to his house, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 afflicted the child that Uriyah’s wife had born to Dawiḏ, and he was sick.
12.16: And Dawiḏ sought Elohim for the child, and Dawiḏ fasted and went in and spent all night lying on the ground.
12.17: So the elders of his house stood up over him, to raise him up from the earth. But he would not, nor did he eat food with them.
12.18: And on the seventh day it came to be that the child died. And the servants of Dawiḏ were afraid to inform him that the child was dead, for they said, “Look, while the child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to our voice. And how do we say to him that the child is dead? He may act terribly!”
12.19: And Dawiḏ saw that his servants were whispering, and Dawiḏ perceived that the child was dead. Then Dawiḏ said to his servants, “Is the child dead?” And they said, “He is dead.”
12.20: Dawiḏ then rose up from the ground, and washed and anointed himself, and changed his garments. And he went into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and bowed himself, then came to his own house, and asked, and they put food before him, so he ate.
12.21: And his servants said to him, “What is this that you have done? You fasted and wept because of the living child, but when the child died, you rose up and ate food.”
12.22: And he said, “While the child was alive I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows whether 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shows favor unto me, and the child shall live?’
12.23: “But now he is dead, why should I fast? Am I able to bring him back again? I am going to him, but he does not return to me.”
12.24: And Dawiḏ comforted Bathsheḇa his wife, and went in to her and lay with her. So she bore a son, and he called his name Shelomoh. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loved him,
12.25: and sent by the hand of Nathan the naḇi, and called his name Yeḏiḏeyah, because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
12.26: And Yo’aḇ fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and captured the royal city.
12.27: And Yo’aḇ sent messengers to Dawiḏ, and said, “I have fought against Rabbah, and I have captured the city’s water supply.
12.28: “And now, gather the rest of the people together and encamp against the city and capture it, lest I capture the city and it be called after my name.”
12.29: And Dawiḏ gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and captured it.
12.30: And he took their meleḵ’s crown from his head. And its weight was a kiḵar of gold, with precious stones, and it was on Dawiḏ’s head. And he brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount.
12.31: And he brought out the people who were in it, and put them to the saw and to sharp instruments of iron and to axes of iron, and made them pass over to the brick works. And so he did with all the cities of the children of Ammon. And Dawiḏ and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.

13.1: And after this it came to be that Aḇshalom son of Dawiḏ had a lovely sister, whose name was Tamar, and Amnon son of Dawiḏ loved her.
13.2: And Amnon was distressed, even to become sick, because of his sister Tamar - for she was a maiden - and it was hard in the eyes of Amnon to do whatever to her.
13.3: And Amnon had a friend whose name was Yonaḏaḇ son of Shim’ah, Dawiḏ’s brother. Now Yonaḏaḇ was a very cunning man.
13.4: And he said to him, “Why are you, the meleḵ’s son, becoming thinner day after day? Explain it to me.” And Amnon said to him, “I love Tamar, my brother Aḇshalom’s sister.”
13.5: And Yonaḏaḇ said to him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me food, and make the food before my eyes so that I see it, and eat it from her hand.’ ”
13.6: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. And when the meleḵ came to see him, Amnon said to the meleḵ, “Please let Tamar my sister come and make a couple of cakes for me before my eyes, so that I eat from her hand.”
13.7: And Dawiḏ sent to Tamar, to the house, saying, “Please go to the house of your brother Amnon, and make food for him.”
13.8: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house, while he was lying down. And she took dough and kneaded it, and made cakes before his eyes, and baked the cakes.
13.9: And she took the pan and turned them out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, “Make everyone go away from me.” And they all went out from him.
13.10: And Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, that I eat from your hand.” And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them to Amnon her brother in the bedroom.
13.11: And she brought them to him to eat, and he took hold of her and said to her, “Come, lie with me, my sister.”
13.12: And she answered him, “No, my brother, do not humble me, for it is not done so in Yisra’ĕl. Do not do this wickedness!
13.13: “And I, where could I take my shame? And you - you would be like one of the fools in Yisra’ĕl. And now, please speak to the meleḵ, for he would not withhold me from you.”
13.14: But he would not listen to her voice, and being stronger than she, he humbled her and lay with her.
13.15: Amnon then exceedingly hated her, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, “Arise, go!”
13.16: And she said to him, “No, for this evil of sending me away is worse than the other you have done to me.” But he would not listen to her.
13.17: And he called his young man serving him, and said, “Now put this one out, away from me, and bolt the door behind her.”
13.18: And she had on a long coat, for the meleḵ’s maiden daughters wore such garments. And his servant put her out and bolted the door behind her.
13.19: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her long coat that was on her, and put her hand on her head and went away crying bitterly.
13.20: And Aḇshalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now, keep silent, my sister. He is your brother, do not take this matter to heart.” So Tamar remained in the house of her brother Aḇshalom, but was ruined.
13.21: And Meleḵ Dawiḏ heard all these reports, and he was very wroth.
13.22: And Aḇshalom spoke to his brother Amnon neither good nor evil. For Aḇshalom hated Amnon, because he had humbled his sister Tamar.
13.23: And it came to be, after two years, that Aḇshalom had sheep-shearers in Ba’al Ḥatsor, which is beside Ephrayim, and Aḇshalom invited all the sons of the meleḵ.
13.24: And Aḇshalom came to the meleḵ and said, “See, your servant has sheep-shearers. Please, let the meleḵ and his servants go with your servant.”
13.25: But the meleḵ said to Aḇshalom, “No, my son, let us not all go now, lest we be too heavy on you.” And he urged him, but he would not go. And he baraḵ him.
13.26: And Aḇshalom said, “If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us.” And the meleḵ said to him, “Why should he go with you?”
13.27: And Aḇshalom urged him, so he let Amnon and all the sons of the meleḵ go with him.
13.28: And Aḇshalom had commanded his servants, saying, “Watch, and when the heart of Amnon is glad with wine, and I shall say to you, ‘Smite Amnon!’ then kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be strong and brave.”
13.29: Then the servants of Aḇshalom did to Amnon as Aḇshalom had commanded. Then all the sons of the meleḵ rose up, and each one mounted his mule and fled.
13.30: And it came to be, while they were on the way, that news came to Dawiḏ, saying, “Aḇshalom has smitten all the sons of the meleḵ, and not one of them is left!”
13.31: And the meleḵ rose up and tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their garments torn.
13.32: And Yonaḏaḇ son of Shim’ah, Dawiḏ’s brother, answered and said, “Do not let my master say they have killed all the young men, the sons of the meleḵ, for only Amnon is dead. For by the command of Aḇshalom this has been appointed from the day that he humbled his sister Tamar.
13.33: “And now, let not my master the meleḵ take the matter to his heart, to think that all the sons of the meleḵ are dead. For only Amnon is dead.”
13.34: And Aḇshalom fled, and the young man who was watching lifted up his eyes and looked and saw many people were coming from the way behind him, on the side of the hill.
13.35: Then Yonaḏaḇ said to the meleḵ, “Look, the sons of the meleḵ are coming; as your servant said, so it is.”
13.36: And it came to be, as soon as he had finished speaking, that look, the sons of the meleḵ came, and they lifted up their voice and wept. And the meleḵ too, and all his servants wept very bitterly.
13.37: But Aḇshalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihuḏ, meleḵ of Geshur. And Dawiḏ mourned for his son all the days.
13.38: So Aḇshalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
13.39: Meleḵ Dawiḏ then longed to go to Aḇshalom, for he had been comforted concerning Amnon, because he was dead.

14.1: And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah knew that the heart of the meleḵ was towards Aḇshalom.
14.2: And Yo’aḇ sent to Teqowa and brought from there a wise woman, and said to her, “Please pretend to be a mourner, and put on mourning garments, and do not anoint yourself with oil, but act like a woman who has been mourning a long time for the dead.
14.3: “Then you shall go to the meleḵ and speak to him according to this word.” And Yo’aḇ put the words in her mouth.
14.4: And when the woman of Teqowa spoke to the meleḵ, she fell on her face to the ground and did obeisance, and said, “Save, O meleḵ!”
14.5: And the meleḵ said to her, “What is your trouble?” And she answered, “Truly I am a widow, my husband is dead.
14.6: “And your female servant had two sons. And the two fought with each other in the field, and there was no one to part them, but the one smote the other and killed him.
14.7: “And see, the entire clan has risen up against your female servant and said, ‘Give him who smote his brother, so that we put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and destroy the heir also.’ Thus they would extinguish my burning coal that is left, and leave to my husband neither name nor remnant on the earth.”
14.8: And the meleḵ said to the woman, “Go to your house, and let me give orders concerning you.”
14.9: And the woman of Teqowa said to the meleḵ, “My master, O meleḵ, let the wickedness be on me and on my father’s house, and the meleḵ and his throne be guiltless.”
14.10: And the meleḵ said, “Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and let him no longer touch you.”
14.11: And she said, “Please let the meleḵ remember 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and the redeemer of blood not destroy any more, lest they destroy my son.” And he said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground.”
14.12: And the woman said, “Please, let your female servant speak a word to my master the meleḵ.” And he said, “Speak.”
14.13: And the woman said, “And why have you reasoned like this against the people of Elohim? For in speaking this word the meleḵ is as one who is guilty, in that the meleḵ does not bring his outcast one home again.
14.14: “For we shall certainly die and become like water spilled on the ground, which is not gathered up again. Yet Elohim does not take away a life, but shall devise ways, so that His outcast ones are not cast out from Him.
14.15: “And now I have come to speak this word to my master the meleḵ because the people have made me afraid. And your female servant said, ‘Please let me speak to the meleḵ, it could be that the meleḵ does what his female servant asks,
14.16: for the meleḵ has listened to deliver his female servant from the hand of the man seeking to destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of Elohim.’
14.17: “Then your female servant said, ‘Please let the word of my master the meleḵ be comforting, for my master the meleḵ is as the messenger of Elohim, in discerning the good and the evil. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim is with you.’ ”
14.18: And the meleḵ answered and said to the woman, “Please do not hide from me the matter that I am asking you.” And the woman said, “Please, let my master the meleḵ speak.”
14.19: And the meleḵ said, “Is the hand of Yo’aḇ with you in all this?” And the woman answered and said, “As your being lives, my master the meleḵ, there is none to the right or to the left from all that my master the meleḵ has spoken. For your servant Yo’aḇ commanded me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your female servant.
14.20: “Your servant Yo’aḇ has done this to change the appearance of the matter. But my master is wise, according to the wisdom of a messenger of Elohim, to know all that is in the earth.”
14.21: And the meleḵ said to Yo’aḇ, “See now, you shall do this matter. And go, bring back the young man Aḇshalom.”
14.22: And Yo’aḇ fell to the ground on his face and did obeisance, and baraḵ the meleḵ. And Yo’aḇ said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my master, O meleḵ, in that the meleḵ has done the word of his servant.”
14.23: And Yo’aḇ rose up and went to Geshur, and brought Aḇshalom to Yerushalayim.
14.24: And the meleḵ said, “Let him return to his own house, but do not let him see my face.” And Aḇshalom went to his own house, and did not see the meleḵ’s face.
14.25: And in all Yisra’ĕl there was no one who was praised as much as Aḇshalom for his good looks. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
14.26: And when he cut the hair of his head - for it was at every year’s end that he cut it because it was heavy on him - when he cut it, he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred sheqels by the meleḵ’s weight.
14.27: And to Aḇshalom were born three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a woman of lovely appearance.
14.28: And Aḇshalom dwelt in Yerushalayim, two years, and he had not seen the meleḵ’s face.
14.29: Then Aḇshalom sent for Yo’aḇ, to send him to the meleḵ, but he would not come to him. And he sent again the second time, but he would not come.
14.30: And he said to his servants, “See, Yo’aḇ’s field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and light it on fire.” And Aḇshalom’s servants lit the field on fire.
14.31: Then Yo’aḇ rose up and came to the house of Aḇshalom, and said to him, “Why have your servants lit my field on fire?”
14.32: And Aḇshalom said to Yo’aḇ, “Look, I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, so that I send you to the meleḵ, to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It was good for me while I was there.” ’ And now, let me see the meleḵ’s face. And if there is any wickedness in me, then you shall put me to death.”
14.33: Yo’aḇ then went to the meleḵ and informed him. And he called for Aḇshalom, and he came to the meleḵ and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the meleḵ. Then the meleḵ kissed Aḇshalom.

15.1: And it came to be after this that Aḇshalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before him.
15.2: And Aḇshalom used to rise early and stand beside the way to the gate. And it came to be, whenever anyone who had a complaint came to the meleḵ for a right-ruling, that Aḇshalom would call to him and say, “What city are you from?” And when he said, “Your servant is from such and such a tribe of Yisra’ĕl,”
15.3: Aḇshalom would say to him, “Look, your matters are good and right, but you have nobody from the meleḵ to hear you.”
15.4: And Aḇshalom would say, “Oh, that I were made judge in the land, and everyone who has any complaint or case would come to me, and I shall let right be done to him.”
15.5: And it came to be, whenever anyone came near him to bow down to him, that he would put out his hand and take him and kiss him.
15.6: And Aḇshalom did this to all Yisra’ĕl who came to the meleḵ for right-ruling. And Aḇshalom stole the hearts of the men of Yisra’ĕl.
15.7: And it came to be at the end of four years that Aḇshalom said to the meleḵ, “Please, let me go to Ḥeḇron and pay the vow which I vowed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.8: “For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelt at Geshur in Aram, saying, ‘If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 indeed brings me back to Yerushalayim, then I shall serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ ”
15.9: And the meleḵ said to him, “Go in peace.” And he rose up and went to Ḥeḇron.
15.10: But Aḇshalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the ram’s horn, then you shall say, ‘Aḇshalom is meleḵ in Ḥeḇron!” ’
15.11: And with Aḇshalom went two hundred men from Yerushalayim who were invited, and they went along unsuspectingly, and did not know the matter at all.
15.12: Aḇshalom also sent for Aḥithophel the Gilonite, counsellor of Dawiḏ, from his city, from Giloh, while he was bringing offerings. And it came to be that the conspiracy became strong, for the people with Aḇshalom kept increasing.
15.13: Then a messenger came to Dawiḏ, saying, “The hearts of the men of Yisra’ĕl are with Aḇshalom.”
15.14: And Dawiḏ said to all his servants who were with him at Yerushalayim, “Rise up, and let us flee, for none of us shall escape from Aḇshalom. Go in haste, lest he overtake us quickly and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.”
15.15: And the meleḵ’s servants said to the meleḵ, “Look, your servants do according to all my master the meleḵ chooses.”
15.16: And the meleḵ went out, and all his household at his feet. But the meleḵ left ten women, concubines, to look after the house.
15.17: So the meleḵ went out, and all the people at his feet, and they stood still at the last house.
15.18: And all his servants were passing on at his side. And all the Kerĕthites, and all the Pelĕthites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had followed him from Gath, were passing on before the meleḵ.
15.19: And the meleḵ said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why do you go, you also, with us? Turn back and remain with the meleḵ, for you are a foreigner, and also an exile from your own place.
15.20: “You came yesterday, and should I today make you wander up and down with us, when I am going wherever I am going? Return, and take your brothers back. Kindness and truth be with you.”
15.21: And Ittai answered the meleḵ and said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, and as my master the meleḵ lives, in whatever place my master the meleḵ is, whether in death or life, let your servant also be there.”
15.22: Therefore Dawiḏ said to Ittai, “Go, and pass over.” And Ittai the Gittite and all his men and all the little ones who were with him passed over.
15.23: And all the land was weeping with a loud voice, and all the people were passing over. And the meleḵ himself was passing over the wadi Qiḏron, and all the people were passing over toward the way of the wilderness.
15.24: And see, Tsaḏoq also, and all the Lĕwites with him, bearing the ark of the Covenant of Elohim. And they put down the ark of Elohim, and Eḇyathar went up until all the people completed passing over from the city.
15.25: And the meleḵ said to Tsaḏoq, “Take the ark of Elohim back to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then He shall bring me back and show me both it and His dwelling.
15.26: “But if He says thus, ‘I have not delighted in you,’ here I am, let Him do to me as is good in His eyes.”
15.27: And the meleḵ said to Tsaḏoq the kohĕn, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Aḥima’ats your son, and Yahonathan son of Eḇyathar.
15.28: “See, I am waiting in the desert plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
15.29: And Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar took the ark of Elohim back to Yerushalayim, and they remained there.
15.30: And Dawiḏ went up by the ascent of the Olives, and wept as he went up. And he had his head covered and went barefoot. And all the people who were with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went up.
15.31: And Dawiḏ was informed, saying, “Aḥithophel is among the conspirators with Aḇshalom.” And Dawiḏ said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I pray You, make the counsel of Aḥithophel foolish!”
15.32: And it came to be that Dawiḏ came to the summit, where he bowed himself before Elohim, and saw Ḥushai the Arkite, came to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
15.33: And Dawiḏ said to him, “If you pass on with me, then you shall become a burden to me,
15.34: but if you return to the city, and say to Aḇshalom, ‘I am your servant, O meleḵ - once servant of your father, but now I am your servant,’ then you shall nullify the counsel of Aḥithophel for me.
15.35: “And are not Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the kohenim with you there? And it shall be that every matter you hear from the meleḵ’s house, you should report to Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the kohenim.
15.36: “See, there with them are their two sons, Aḥima’ats, Tsaḏoq’s son, and Yahonathan, Eḇyathar’s son. And by them you shall send me every matter you hear.”
15.37: And Ḥushai, Dawiḏ’s friend, went into the city. And Aḇshalom came into Yerushalayim.

16.1: And Dawiḏ had passed on a little from the summit, and saw Tsiḇa the servant of Mephiḇosheth, who met him with a couple of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves, and one hundred cakes of raisins, and one hundred summer fruit, and a skin of wine.
16.2: And the meleḵ said to Tsiḇa, “Why do you have these?” And Tsiḇa said, “The donkeys are for the meleḵ’s household to ride on, and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for the wearied to drink in the wilderness.”
16.3: And the meleḵ said, “And where is the son of your master?” And Tsiḇa said to the meleḵ, “See, he remains in Yerushalayim, for he said, ‘Today the house of Yisra’ĕl is going to return the reign of my father to me.’ ”
16.4: And the meleḵ said to Tsiḇa, “See, all that belongs to Mephiḇosheth is yours.” And Tsiḇa said, “I have bowed myself, let me find favor in your eyes, my master, O meleḵ!”
16.5: And when Meleḵ Dawiḏ came to Baḥurim he saw a man from the clan of the house of Sha’ul, whose name was Shim’i son of Gĕra, coming from there. He came out, cursing as he came.
16.6: And he threw stones at Dawiḏ. And all the servants of Meleḵ Dawiḏ, and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on his left.
16.7: And this is what Shim’i said as he cursed, “Get out! Get out! O man of blood, and man of Beliya’al!
16.8: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has brought upon you all the blood of the house of Sha’ul, in whose place you have reigned. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given the reign into the hand of Aḇshalom your son. And see, you are in your own evil, for you are a man of blood!”
16.9: And Aḇishai son of Tseruyah said to the meleḵ, “Why should this dead dog curse my master the meleḵ? Please, let me pass over and take off his head!”
16.10: And the meleḵ said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Tseruyah? For let him curse, even because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said to him, ‘Curse Dawiḏ.’ And who should say, ‘Why did you do that?’ ”
16.11: And Dawiḏ said to Aḇishai and all his servants, “See how my son who came from my own body seeks my life, and how much more now this Binyamite? Leave him alone, and let him curse, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken to him.
16.12: “If so be, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks on my affliction, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall return good to me for his cursing today.”
16.13: And as Dawiḏ and his men went in the way, Shim’i walked alongside him on the hillside, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him and kicked up dust.
16.14: And the meleḵ and all the people who were with him became weary, and they refreshed themselves there.
16.15: And Aḇshalom and all the people, the men of Yisra’ĕl, came to Yerushalayim, and Aḥithophel was with him.
16.16: And it came to be, when Ḥushai the Arkite, the friend of Dawiḏ, had come to Aḇshalom, that Ḥushai said to Aḇshalom, “Let the meleḵ live! Let the meleḵ live!”
16.17: And Aḇshalom said to Ḥushai, “Is this your kindness to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?”
16.18: And Ḥushai said to Aḇshalom, “No, I am for the one whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and this people and all the men of Yisra’ĕl have chosen, and with him I remain.
16.19: “And besides, whom should I serve? Should it not be before his son? As I have served before your father, so I am before you.”
16.20: And Aḇshalom said to Aḥithophel, “Give your advice. What should we do?”
16.21: And Aḥithophel said to Aḇshalom, “Go in to your father’s concubines, whom he has left to look after the house. And all Yisra’ĕl shall hear that you have made yourself a stench to your father. And the hands of all who are with you shall be strong.”
16.22: So they pitched a tent for Aḇshalom on the top of the house, and Aḇshalom went in to his father’s concubines before the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl.
16.23: Now the advice Aḥithophel gave in those days was as if one had inquired at the word of Elohim. So was all the advice of Aḥithophel both to Dawiḏ and to Aḇshalom.

17.1: And Aḥithophel said to Aḇshalom, “Please let me choose twelve thousand men, and let me arise and pursue Dawiḏ tonight,
17.2: and come upon him while he is weary and weak. And I shall make him afraid and all the people who are with him shall flee. And I shall smite the meleḵ alone,
17.3: and bring back all the people to you. When all return except the man whom you seek, all the people should be at peace.”
17.4: And the saying pleased Aḇshalom and all the elders of Yisra’ĕl.
17.5: But Aḇshalom said, “Now call Ḥushai the Arkite also, and let us hear what he says too.”
17.6: And Ḥushai came to Aḇshalom, and Aḇshalom spoke to him, saying, “Aḥithophel has spoken according to this word. Should we do as he says? If not, speak up.”
17.7: And Ḥushai said to Aḇshalom, “The advice that Aḥithophel has given is not good at this time.”
17.8: And Ḥushai said, “You know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are as bitter in being as a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. And your father is a man of battle, and would not spend the night with the people.
17.9: “See, by now he is hidden in some pit, or in some place. And it shall be, when some of them fall at the first, that whoever hears it shall say, ‘There has been a smiting among the people who are following Aḇshalom.’
17.10: “And even he who is brave, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, would utterly melt. For all Yisra’ĕl knows that your father is a mighty man, and those who are with him are brave men.
17.11: “But I advise: Let all Yisra’ĕl without fail be gathered to you, from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa, as numerous as the sand by the sea, and that you yourself go to battle.
17.12: “And we shall come upon him in some place where he is found, and fall on him as the dew falls on the ground. And there shall be left of him and of all the men with him not even one.
17.13: “And if he withdraws into a city, then all Yisra’ĕl shall bring ropes to that city. And we shall pull it into the wadi, until there is not one small stone found there.”
17.14: Aḇshalom and all the men of Yisra’ĕl then said, “The advice of Ḥushai the Arkite is better than the advice of Aḥithophel.” For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had ordained to nullify the good advice of Aḥithophel, for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 bringing evil upon Aḇshalom.
17.15: Ḥushai then said to Tsaḏoq and to Eḇyathar the kohenim, “Aḥithophel has advised Aḇshalom and the elders of Yisra’ĕl such and such, but I have advised so and so.
17.16: “And now, send hastily and inform Dawiḏ, saying, ‘Do not spend this night in the desert plains of the wilderness, but pass over without fail, lest the meleḵ and all the people with him be swallowed up.’ ”
17.17: And Yahonathan and Aḥima’ats were stationed at Ĕyn Roḡĕl, and a female servant would come and inform them, and they would go and inform Meleḵ Dawiḏ, for they could not be seen entering the city.
17.18: But a youth saw them, and informed Aḇshalom. So the two of them went away at once and came to a man’s house in Baḥurim, who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it.
17.19: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground grain on it, so the matter was not known.
17.20: And the servants of Aḇshalom came to the woman at the house and said, “Where are Aḥima’ats and Yahonathan?” And the woman said to them, “They have passed over the stream of water.” And they looked and did not find them, and returned to Yerushalayim.
17.21: And it came to be, after they had left, that they came up out of the well and went and informed Meleḵ Dawiḏ, and said to Dawiḏ, “Arise and pass over the water quickly. For thus Aḥithophel has advised against you.”
17.22: And Dawiḏ and all the people who were with him rose up and passed over the Yardĕn. And by morning light not even one remained who had not gone over the Yardĕn.
17.23: And Aḥithophel saw that his advice was not followed, so he saddled his donkey, and rose up and went home to his house, to his city. Then he gave charge to his house, and hanged himself, and died. And he was buried in his father’s tomb.
17.24: And Dawiḏ came to Maḥanayim. And Aḇshalom passed over the Yardĕn, he and all the men of Yisra’ĕl with him.
17.25: And Aḇshalom appointed Amasa over the army instead of Yo’aḇ. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Yithra, an Yisra’ĕlite, who had gone in to Aḇiḡayil the daughter of Naḥash, sister of Tseruyah, Yo’aḇ’s mother.
17.26: And Yisra’ĕl and Aḇshalom encamped in the land of Gil’aḏ.
17.27: And it came to be, when Dawiḏ had come to Maḥanayim, that Shoḇi son of Naḥash from Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Maḵir son of Ammi’ĕl from Lo Ḏeḇar, and Barzillai the Gil’aḏite from Roḡelim,
17.28: brought beds and basins, and earthen vessels and wheat, and barley and flour, and roasted grain and beans, and lentils, and parched grain,
17.29: and honey and curds, and sheep and cheese of the herd, for Dawiḏ and the people who were with him to eat. For they said, “The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.”

18.1: And Dawiḏ mustered the people who were with him, and put commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds over them.
18.2: And Dawiḏ sent out one third of the people under the hand of Yo’aḇ, and one third under the hand of Aḇishai son of Tseruyah, Yo’aḇ’s brother, and one third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the meleḵ said to the people, “I shall certainly go out with you too.”
18.3: But the people answered, “Do not go out, for if we flee away, they would not lay heart upon us. Even if half of us die, they would not lay heart upon us. For now, ten thousand are like us. Therefore, it is better for you to support us from the city.”
18.4: And the meleḵ said to them, “That which is good in your eyes I do.” And the meleḵ stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.
18.5: And the meleḵ ordered Yo’aḇ, and Aḇishai and Ittai, saying, “Be gentle with the young man Aḇshalom for my sake.” And all the people heard when the meleḵ gave all the commanders orders concerning Aḇshalom.
18.6: So the people went out into the field to meet Yisra’ĕl. And the battle was in the forest of Ephrayim,
18.7: and the people of Yisra’ĕl were smitten there before the servants of Dawiḏ. And the smiting there that day was great - twenty thousand.
18.8: And the battle there was scattered over the face of all the land, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.
18.9: And when Aḇshalom met the servants of Dawiḏ, Aḇshalom was riding on a mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of a great terebinth tree, and his head caught in the terebinth. And he was suspended between the shamayim and earth while the mule which was under him passed on.
18.10: And a certain man saw it and informed Yo’aḇ, and said, “Look, I saw Aḇshalom hanging in a terebinth tree!”
18.11: And Yo’aḇ said to the man who informed him, “Now look, you saw, and why did you not smite him to the earth there? Then I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a belt.”
18.12: But the man answered Yo’aḇ, “Though I were to receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I would not raise my hand against the son of the meleḵ. Because in our hearing the meleḵ ordered you and Aḇishai and Ittai, saying, ‘Take heed, you who go against the youth, against Aḇshalom!’
18.13: “Otherwise I would have been untrue to my own life. For no matter is hidden from the meleḵ, and you yourself would have put yourself against me.”
18.14: And Yo’aḇ said, “Let me not waste time here with you.” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through Aḇshalom’s heart, while he was still alive in the midst of the terebinth tree.
18.15: And ten young men who bore Yo’aḇ’s armor went around, and smote Aḇshalom and put him to death.
18.16: And Yo’aḇ blew the ram’s horn, and the people returned from pursuing Yisra’ĕl, for Yo’aḇ had held the people back.
18.17: And they took Aḇshalom and threw him into a large pit in the forest, and heaped a very large pile of stones over him. And all Yisra’ĕl fled, each one to his tent.
18.18: And Aḇshalom in his lifetime had taken and put up a monument for himself, which is in the Meleḵ’s Valley. For he said, “I have no son to keep my name in remembrance.” And he called the monument after his own name. And to this day it is called Aḇshalom’s Monument.
18.19: And Aḥima’ats son of Tsaḏoq said, “Please let me run and take the news to the meleḵ, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has judged his enemies.”
18.20: But Yo’aḇ said to him, “You are not the man to take the news today, but you shall take the news another day. But today you do not take news, because the meleḵ’s son is dead.”
18.21: And Yo’aḇ said to the Kushite, “Go, inform the meleḵ what you have seen.” And the Kushite bowed himself to Yo’aḇ and ran.
18.22: And Aḥima’ats son of Tsaḏoq said again to Yo’aḇ, “And whatever might be, please let me also run after the Kushite.” And Yo’aḇ said, “Why would you run, my son, there is no news to bring you reward.”
18.23: “But whatever might be, let me run.” So he said to him, “Run.” And Aḥima’ats ran by the way of the plain, and passed the Kushite.
18.24: Now Dawiḏ was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof over the gate, to the wall, and lifted his eyes and looked and saw a man, running alone.
18.25: So the watchman called out and told the meleḵ. And the meleḵ said, “If he is alone, there is news in his mouth.” And he came nearer and nearer.
18.26: And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called out to the gatekeeper and said, “See, a man, running by himself!” And the meleḵ said, “This one is also bringing news.”
18.27: And the watchman said, “I see the running of the first is like the running of Aḥima’ats son of Tsaḏoq.” And the meleḵ said, “This is a good man, and he comes with good news.”
18.28: And Aḥima’ats called out and said to the meleḵ, “Peace!” Then he bowed down with his face to the earth before the meleḵ, and said, “Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who has surrendered the men who raised their hand against my master the meleḵ!”
18.29: And the meleḵ said, “Peace to the young man, to Aḇshalom?” And Aḥima’ats answered, “When Yo’aḇ sent the meleḵ’s servant and me your servant, I saw a great crowd, but I did not know why.”
18.30: And the meleḵ said, “Turn aside and stand here.” And he turned aside and stood still.
18.31: And see, the Kushite came, and the Kushite said, “Receive news, my master the meleḵ! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has judged this day all those who rose against you.”
18.32: And the meleḵ said to the Kushite, “Peace to the young man, to Aḇshalom?” And the Kushite answered, “Let the enemies of my master the meleḵ, and all who rise against you for evil, be as that young man is!”
18.33: And the meleḵ was shaken, and went up to the room over the gate, and wept. And as he went, he said this, “O my son Aḇshalom! My son, my son Aḇshalom, if only I had died instead of you! O Aḇshalom my son, my son!”

19.1: And it was reported to Yo’aḇ, “See, the meleḵ is weeping and mourning for Aḇshalom.”
19.2: So the deliverance that day was turned into mourning for all the people. For the people heard on that day, saying, “The meleḵ has been grieved for his son.”
19.3: And the people stole back into the city that day, as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
19.4: And the meleḵ covered his face, and the meleḵ cried out with a loud voice, “O my son Aḇshalom! O Aḇshalom, my son, my son!”
19.5: And Yo’aḇ came into the house to the meleḵ, and said, “Today you have put to shame all your servants who today have saved your life, and the lives of your sons and daughters, and the lives of your wives and the lives of your concubines,
19.6: by loving those who hate you, and by hating those who love you. For you have made it clear today that you have neither commanders nor servants, for today I know that if Aḇshalom had lived and all of us had died today, then it would be right in your eyes.
19.7: “And now, arise, go out and speak to the heart of your servants. For I swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, if you do not go out, not one passes the night with you. And that is worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now.”
19.8: So the meleḵ rose up and sat in the gate. And they told all the people, saying, “Look, the meleḵ is sitting in the gate.” And all the people came before the meleḵ. As for Yisra’ĕl, they had fled, each one to his tent.
19.9: And it came to be, that all the people were contending throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “The meleḵ delivered us from the hand of the enemies, he rescued us from the hand of the Pelishtites, and now he has fled from the land because of Aḇshalom,
19.10: and Aḇshalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. And now, why are you silent about bringing back the meleḵ?”
19.11: And Meleḵ Dawiḏ sent to Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the kohenim, saying, “Speak to the elders of Yahuḏah, saying, ‘Why are you the last to bring the meleḵ back to his house, since the words of all Yisra’ĕl have come to the meleḵ, to his house?
19.12: ‘You are my brothers, you are my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the last to bring back the meleḵ?’
19.13: “And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? Elohim do so to me, and more also, if you are not commander of the army before me all the days in place of Yo’aḇ.’ ”
19.14: Thus he swayed the hearts of all the men of Yahuḏah as one man, so that they sent to the meleḵ, “Return, you and all your servants!”
19.15: So the meleḵ returned and came to the Yardĕn. And Yahuḏah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the meleḵ, to bring the meleḵ over the Yardĕn.
19.16: And Shim’i son of Gĕra, a Binyamite, who was from Baḥurim, hastened and came down with the men of Yahuḏah to meet Meleḵ Dawiḏ.
19.17: And with him were a thousand men of Binyamin, and Tsiḇa the servant of the house of Sha’ul, and his fifteen sons, and his twenty servants with him. And they rushed over the Yardĕn before the meleḵ.
19.18: And they passed over the ford to bring over the meleḵ’s household, and to do what was good in his eyes. And Shim’i son of Gĕra fell down before the meleḵ when he had passed over the Yardĕn,
19.19: and said to the meleḵ, “Do not let my master reckon wickedness to me, neither remember what wickedness your servant did on the day that my master the meleḵ left Yerushalayim, that the meleḵ should take it to heart.
19.20: “For I, your servant, know that I have sinned. And see, I have come today, first of all the house of Yosĕph, to go down to meet my master the meleḵ.”
19.21: But Aḇishai son of Tseruyah answered and said, “Should Shim’i not be put to death for this, because he cursed the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
19.22: And Dawiḏ said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Tseruyah, that you are to be adversaries to me today? Should any man be put to death in Yisra’ĕl today? For do I not know that I am meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl today?”
19.23: So the meleḵ said to Shim’i, “You do not die.” And the meleḵ swore to him.
19.24: And Mephiḇosheth son of Sha’ul came down to meet the meleḵ. And he had not attended to his feet, nor trimmed his moustache, nor washed his garments, from the day the meleḵ went away until the day he came back in peace.
19.25: And it came to be, when he had come to Yerushalayim to meet the meleḵ, that the meleḵ said to him, “Why did you not go with me, Mephiḇosheth?”
19.26: And he answered, “My master, O meleḵ, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, ‘I am saddling a donkey for myself to ride on it and go to the meleḵ,’ because your servant is lame.
19.27: “And he spoke slander against your servant to my master the meleḵ, but my master the meleḵ is as a messenger of Elohim. Therefore do what is good in your eyes.
19.28: “For all of my father’s house were but dead men before my master the meleḵ. Yet you put your servant among those who eat at your own table. Therefore what right have I still to cry out any more to the meleḵ?”
19.29: Then the meleḵ said to him, “Why do you speak any more of your matters? I have said, ‘You and Tsiḇa share the land.’ ”
19.30: And Mephiḇosheth said to the meleḵ, “Rather, let him take it all, since my master the meleḵ has come back in peace to his own house.
19.31: And Barzillai the Gil’aḏite came down from Roḡelim and passed over the Yardĕn with the meleḵ, to send him on his way over the Yardĕn.
19.32: And Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. And he had sustained the meleḵ while he was dwelling at Maḥanayim, for he was a very rich man.
19.33: And the meleḵ said to Barzillai, “Pass over with me, and I shall provide for you with me in Yerushalayim.”
19.34: But Barzillai said to the meleḵ, “How many are the days of my life, that I should go up with the meleḵ to Yerushalayim?
19.35: “I am now eighty years old. Do I discern between the good and evil? Does your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Do I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a further burden to my master the meleḵ?
19.36: “Your servant would only pass over the Yardĕn with the meleḵ for a short distance. And why should the meleḵ repay me with such a reward?
19.37: “Please let your servant turn back again to die in my own city, near the burying-place of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham, let him pass over with my master the meleḵ, and do for him what is good in your eyes.”
19.38: And the meleḵ answered, “Kimham is passing over with me, and let me do for him what is good in your eyes. Now whatever you choose of me, I do for you.”
19.39: Then all the people went over the Yardĕn. And when the meleḵ had passed over, the meleḵ kissed Barzillai and baraḵ him, and he returned to his own place.
19.40: And the meleḵ passed over to Gilgal, and Kimham passed over with him. And all the people of Yahuḏah brought the meleḵ over, and also half the people of Yisra’ĕl.
19.41: And see, all the men of Yisra’ĕl were coming to the meleḵ! And they said to the meleḵ, “Why have our brothers, the men of Yahuḏah, stolen you away and brought the meleḵ, and his household, and all Dawiḏ’s men with him over the Yardĕn?”
19.42: And all the men of Yahuḏah answered the men of Yisra’ĕl, “Because the meleḵ is our relative. And why are you displeased over this matter? Have we at all eaten at the meleḵ’s cost? Or has he given us any gift?”
19.43: And the men of Yisra’ĕl answered the men of Yahuḏah, and said, “We have ten parts in the meleḵ, and in Dawiḏ too, we have more than you. Why then did you despise us? Was it not our advice first to bring back our meleḵ?” But the words of the men of Yahuḏah were harsher than the words of the men of Yisra’ĕl.

2.1: And it came to be afterwards that Dawiḏ inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “Do I go up to any of the cities of Yahuḏah?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, “Go up.” And Dawiḏ said, “Where should I go up?” And He said, “To Ḥeḇron.”
2.2: And Dawiḏ went up there, as well as his two wives, Aḥino’am the Yizre’ĕlitess, and Aḇiḡayil the widow of Naḇal the Karmelite.
2.3: And Dawiḏ brought up the men who were with him, each man with his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Ḥeḇron.
2.4: And the men of Yahuḏah came, and anointed Dawiḏ meleḵ over the house of Yahuḏah there. They also reported to Dawiḏ, saying, “The men of Yaḇĕsh Gil’aḏ are they who buried Sha’ul.”
2.5: Dawiḏ then sent messengers to the men of Yaḇĕsh Gil’aḏ, and said to them, “You are beruḵim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for you have shown this kindness to your master, to Sha’ul, that you buried him.
2.6: “And now, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 show kindness and truth to you, and I am also going to do you good, because you have done this deed.
2.7: “And now, let your hands be strengthened and be brave, for your master Sha’ul is dead, and also the house of Yahuḏah has anointed me meleḵ over them.”
2.8: But Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, commander of the army of Sha’ul, took Ishbosheth the son of Sha’ul, and brought him over to Maḥanayim,
2.9: and appointed him to reign over Gil’aḏ, and over the Ashĕrites, and over Yizre’ĕl, and over Ephrayim, and over Binyamin, and over all Yisra’ĕl.
2.10: Ishbosheth, son of Sha’ul, was forty years old when he began to reign over Yisra’ĕl, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Yahuḏah followed Dawiḏ.
2.11: And the time that Dawiḏ was meleḵ in Ḥeḇron over the house of Yahuḏah was seven years and six months.
2.12: And Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, and the servants of Ishbosheth son of Sha’ul, went out from Maḥanayim to Giḇ’on.
2.13: And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah, and the servants of Dawiḏ, went out and met them by the pool of Giḇ’on. And they sat down, one on one side of the pool and the other on the other side of the pool.
2.14: And Aḇnĕr said to Yo’aḇ, “Let the young men now rise and compete before us.” And Yo’aḇ said, “Let them rise.”
2.15: And they rose and went over by number, twelve from Binyamin, followers of Ishbosheth son of Sha’ul, and twelve from the servants of Dawiḏ.
2.16: And each one grasped his opponent by the head and thrust his sword in his opponent’s side, and they fell down together. So that place was called the Field of Sharp Swords, which is in Giḇ’on.
2.17: And the battle was fierce that day, and Aḇnĕr and the men of Yisra’ĕl were smitten before the servants of Dawiḏ.
2.18: And there were three sons of Tseruyah there, Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai and Asah’ĕl. And Asah’ĕl was light on his feet, as one of the gazelles in the field.
2.19: And Asah’ĕl pursued Aḇnĕr, and in going he did not turn aside to the right or to the left from following Aḇnĕr.
2.20: And Aḇnĕr looked behind him and said, “Are you Asah’ĕl?” And he answered, “I am.”
2.21: And Aḇnĕr said to him, “Turn aside to your right hand or to your left, and lay hold on one of the young men and take his armor for yourself.” But Asah’ĕl would not turn aside from following him.
2.22: And Aḇnĕr again said to Asah’ĕl, “Turn aside from following me. Why should I smite you to the ground? How then could I face your brother Yo’aḇ?”
2.23: But he refused to turn aside, and Aḇnĕr smote him with the blunt end of the spear in the stomach, so that the spear came out of his back. And he fell down there and died on the spot. And it came to be that as many as came to the place where Asah’ĕl fell down and died, stood still.
2.24: And Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai pursued Aḇnĕr. And the sun was going down and they came to the hill of Ammah, which overlooks Giyaḥ by the way to the Wilderness of Giḇ’on.
2.25: And the children of Binyamin gathered together behind Aḇnĕr and became a single company, and took their stand on top of a hill.
2.26: And Aḇnĕr called to Yo’aḇ and said, “Should the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it is bitter in the latter end? And when are you going to say to the people to turn back from pursuing their brothers?”
2.27: And Yo’aḇ said, “As Elohim lives, if you had not spoken, then all the people would have given up pursuing their brothers only the next morning.”
2.28: Yo’aḇ then blew a ram’s horn, and all the people halted and pursued Yisra’ĕl no further, nor did they fight any more.
2.29: And Aḇnĕr and his men went on all that night through the desert plain, and passed over the Yardĕn, and went through all Bithron. And they came to Maḥanayim.
2.30: And Yo’aḇ turned back from pursuing Aḇnĕr. And when he had gathered all the people together, there were missing of Dawiḏ’s servants nineteen men and Asah’ĕl.
2.31: But the servants of Dawiḏ had smitten, of Binyamin and Aḇnĕr’s men, three hundred and sixty men who died.
2.32: And they brought Asah’ĕl and buried him in his father’s tomb, which was in Bĕyth Leḥem. And Yo’aḇ and his men went all night, and they came to Ḥeḇron at daybreak.

20.1: And there came to be a man of Beliya’al, whose name was Sheḇa son of Biḵri, a Binyamite. And he blew a ram’s horn, and said, “We have no part in Dawiḏ, nor do we have inheritance in the son of Yishai - each one to his tents, O Yisra’ĕl!”
20.2: Then all the men of Yisra’ĕl deserted Dawiḏ, to follow Sheḇa the son of Biḵri. But the men of Yahuḏah, from the Yardĕn as far as Yerushalayim, clung to their meleḵ.
20.3: And Dawiḏ came to his house at Yerushalayim. And the meleḵ took the ten women, his concubines whom he had left to look after the house, and put them in a protected house and supported them, but did not go in to them. So they were shut up to the day of their death, living in widowhood.
20.4: And the meleḵ said to Amasa, “Call the men of Yahuḏah for me within three days, and be present here yourself.”
20.5: And Amasa went to call the men of Yahuḏah. But he delayed longer than the appointed time which Dawiḏ had appointed him.
20.6: And Dawiḏ said to Aḇishai, “Now Sheḇa son of Biḵri is going to do us more evil than Aḇshalom. Take the servants of your master, and pursue him, lest he find for himself walled cities, and escape us.”
20.7: Then the men of Yo’aḇ went out after him, with the Kerĕthites and the Pelĕthites, and all the mighty men. And they went out of Yerushalayim to pursue Sheḇa son of Biḵri.
20.8: When they were near the large stone which is in Giḇ’on, Amasa came before them. And Yo’aḇ was dressed in battle armor, and on it was a girdle with a sword fastened in its sheath at his hips. And as he went forward, it fell out.
20.9: And Yo’aḇ said to Amasa, “Peace, my brother?” And Yo’aḇ took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.
20.10: But Amasa was not on guard against the sword in Yo’aḇ’s hand. And he struck him with it in the stomach, and his inward parts poured out on the ground, and he did not do so again, and he died. Then Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai his brother pursued Sheḇa son of Biḵri.
20.11: And a man, one of Yo’aḇ’s men, stood beside him, and said, “Whoever is well pleased with Yo’aḇ and whoever is for Dawiḏ, let him follow Yo’aḇ!”
20.12: And Amasa was rolling in his blood in the middle of the highway. And the man saw that all the people stood still, so he moved Amasa from the highway to the field and threw a garment over him, when he saw that everyone who came upon him halted.
20.13: When he was removed from the highway, all the men passed on after Yo’aḇ to pursue Sheḇa son of Biḵri.
20.14: And he passed over through all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl to Aḇĕl, and to Bĕyth Ma’aḵah, and to all the Bĕrites. And they were assembled and went after him too.
20.15: And they went and besieged him in Aḇĕl of Bĕyth Ma’aḵah, and they cast up a siege mound against the city. And it stood in a rampart, and all the people who were with Yo’aḇ battered the wall to throw it down.
20.16: Then a wise woman called out from the city, “Listen, listen! Please say to Yo’aḇ, ‘Come nearby, so that I speak to you.’ ”
20.17: And he came near to her, and the woman said, “Are you Yo’aḇ?” And he answered, “I am.” Then she said to him, “Listen to the words of your female servant.” And he answered, “I am listening.”
20.18: Then she spoke, saying, “In former times they often spoke, saying, ‘Let them inquire of Aḇĕl,’ and so it ended.
20.19: “I am of the peaceable and trustworthy ones in Yisra’ĕl. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Yisra’ĕl. Why do you swallow up the inheritance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
20.20: And Yo’aḇ answered and said, “Far be it, far be it from me to swallow up or to destroy!
20.21: “That is not the case. But a man from the mountains of Ephrayim, Sheḇa son of Biḵri by name, has raised his hand against the meleḵ, against Dawiḏ. Hand him over, him alone, and I withdraw from the city.” And the woman said to Yo’aḇ, “Look, his head is going to be thrown to you over the wall.”
20.22: So the woman in her wisdom went to all the people. And they cut off the head of Sheḇa son of Biḵri, and threw it out to Yo’aḇ. Then he blew a ram’s horn, and they dispersed from the city, each one to his tent. And Yo’aḇ returned to the meleḵ at Yerushalayim.
20.23: Now Yo’aḇ was over all the army of Yisra’ĕl, and Benayah son of Yahoyaḏa was over the Kerĕthites and the Pelĕthites,
20.24: and Aḏoram was over the compulsory labor, and Yahoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder,
20.25: and Shewa was scribe, and Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar were the kohenim,
20.26: and Ira the Ya’irite was kohĕn to Dawiḏ.

21.1: And there was a scarcity of food in the days of Dawiḏ for three years, year after year. And Dawiḏ sought the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answered, “Because of Sha’ul and his bloodthirsty house, because he killed the Giḇ’onites.”
21.2: The meleḵ therefore called the Giḇ’onites and spoke to them. Now the Giḇ’onites were not of the children of Yisra’ĕl, but of the remnant of the Amorites. And the children of Yisra’ĕl had sworn protection to them, but Sha’ul had sought to kill them in his ardor for the children of Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah.
21.3: So Dawiḏ said to the Giḇ’onites, “What should I do for you? And with what do I make atonement, so that you baraḵ the inheritance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
21.4: And the Giḇ’onites said to him, “It is no matter of silver or gold between us and Sha’ul, or his house, neither is it for us to put to death any man in Yisra’ĕl.” And he said, “Whatever you say I do for you.”
21.5: And they said to the meleḵ, “The man who consumed us and plotted against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in all the border of Yisra’ĕl,
21.6: let seven men of his sons be given to us, and we shall hang them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Giḇ’ah of Sha’ul, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chose.” And the meleḵ said, “I give them.”
21.7: But the meleḵ spared Mephiḇosheth son of Yahonathan, son of Sha’ul, because of the oath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that was between them, between Dawiḏ and Yahonathan son of Sha’ul.
21.8: And the meleḵ took the two sons of Ritspah the daughter of Ayah, whom she bore to Sha’ul: Armoni and Mephiḇosheth, and the five sons of Miḵal the daughter of Sha’ul, whom she brought up for Aḏri’ĕl the son of Barzillai, the Meḥolathite,
21.9: and gave them into the hands of the Giḇ’onites, and they hanged them on the hill before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. So the seven fell together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.
21.10: And Ritspah the daughter of Ayah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until the late rains poured on them from the shamayim. And she did not allow the birds of the shamayim to rest on them by day nor the beasts of the field by night.
21.11: And Dawiḏ was informed what Ritspah the daughter of Ayah, the concubine of Sha’ul, had done.
21.12: And Dawiḏ went and took the bones of Sha’ul, and the bones of Yahonathan his son, from the men of Yaḇĕsh Gil’aḏ who had stolen them from the street of Bĕyth Shan, where the Pelishtites had hung them up, after the Pelishtites had struck down Sha’ul in Gilboa.
21.13: And he brought up the bones of Sha’ul and the bones of Yahonathan his son from there, and they gathered the bones of those who had been hanged,
21.14: and buried the bones of Sha’ul and Yahonathan his son in the land of Binyamin in Tsela, in the tomb of Qish his father, and did all that the meleḵ commanded. And after that Elohim heard prayer for the land.
21.15: And the Pelishtites were again fighting against Yisra’ĕl, so Dawiḏ and his servants with him went down and fought against the Pelishtites. And Dawiḏ was weary,
21.16: and Yishbo Benoḇ - who was one of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose bronze spear was three hundred pieces, who was bearing a new sword - spoke of killing Dawiḏ.
21.17: But Aḇishai son of Tseruyah came to help him, and smote the Pelishtite and killed him. Then Dawiḏ’s men swore to him, saying, “Do not go out with us to battle any more, lest you put out the lamp of Yisra’ĕl.”
21.18: And it came to be afterward, that there was a battle again with the Pelishtites at Goḇ. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite smote Saph, who was one of the sons of the giant.
21.19: And there was a battle with the Pelishtites again at Goḇ, where Elḥanan son of Ya’arĕy-Oreḡim the Bĕyth Leḥemite smote Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
21.20: And there was a battle in Gath again, where there was a man of great height, who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. And he also was descended from the giants.
21.21: And he reproached Yisra’ĕl, and Yahonathan son of Shim’i, the brother of Dawiḏ, smote him.
21.22: These four were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of Dawiḏ and by the hand of his servants.

22.1: Then Dawiḏ spoke to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the words of this song, on the day when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Sha’ul.
22.2: And he said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is my rock and my stronghold and my deliverer.
22.3:
“My Elohim is my rock, 
I take refuge in Him, 
My shield and the horn of my deliverance, 
My high tower and my refuge. 
My Savior, You save me from violence.
22.4:
“I call on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the One to be praised, 
And I am saved from my enemies.
22.5:
“For the waves of death surrounded me, 
Floods of Beliya’al made me afraid,
22.6:
“The cords of the grave were all around me; 
The snares of death were before me.
22.7:
“In my distress I called upon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And to my Elohim I cried. 
And from His Hĕyḵal He heard my voice, 
And my cry was in His ears.
22.8:
“And the earth shook and trembled, 
The foundations of the shamayim were troubled, 
Because He was wroth.
22.10:
“And He bowed the shamayim and came down, 
And dense cloud was under His feet.
22.11:
“And He rode upon a keruḇ, and flew, 
And was seen upon the wings of the wind.
22.12:
“And He put darkness around Him as booths, 
Gatherings of waters, thick clouds.
22.13: “From the brightness before Him Coals of fire were kindled.
22.14:
“𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 thundered from the shamayim, 
And the Most High sent forth His voice.
22.15:
“And He sent out arrows and scattered them, 
Lightning, and confused them.
22.16:
“And the channels of the sea were seen, 
The foundations of the world were uncovered 
At the rebuke of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
At the blast of the breath of His nostrils.
22.17:
“He sent from above, He took me, 
He drew me out of many waters.
22.18:
“He delivered me from my strong enemy, 
From those hating me, 
For they were stronger than I.
22.19:
“They confronted me in the day of my calamity, 
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was my support.
22.20:
“And He brought me out into a large place, 
He delivered me for He delighted in me.
22.21:
“𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rewarded me according to my righteousness; 
According to the cleanness of my hands He repaid me.
22.22:
“For I have guarded the Ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And have not acted wickedly against my Elohim.
22.23:
“For all His Right-Rulings are before me; 
As for His Laws, I do not turn from them.
22.24:
“And I am perfect before Him, 
And I guard myself from my wickedness.
22.25:
“And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 repays me according to my righteousness, 
According to my cleanness before His eyes.
22.26:
“With the kind You show Yourself kind, 
With the perfect one You show Yourself perfect,
22.27:
“With the clean You show Yourself clean, 
And with the wicked You show Yourself twisted.
22.28:
“For You save the humble people, 
But Your eyes are on the haughty to bring them low.
22.29:
“For You are my lamp, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 makes my darkness light.
22.30:
“For with You I run against a band, 
With my Elohim I leap over a wall.
22.32:
“For who is Ĕl, besides 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? 
And who is a rock, besides our Elohim?
22.33:
“Ĕl is my mighty stronghold, 
And He makes my way perfect,
22.34:
“Making my feet like the feet of a deer, 
And puts me on my high places,
22.35:
“Teaching my hands for battle, 
So that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
22.36:
“And You give me the shield of Your deliverance, 
And Your lowliness makes me great.
22.37:
“You enlarge my step under me, 
So that my feet shall not slip.
22.38:
“I pursue my enemies and destroy them, 
And I do not turn back till they are destroyed.
22.39:
“And I destroy them and crush them, 
So that they do not rise, 
And fall under my feet.
22.40:
“And You gird me with strength for battle, 
You cause my adversaries to bow under me.
22.41:
“And You make my enemies turn their backs, 
Those hating me, and I cut them off.
22.42:
“They look but there is no savior, 
Unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but He shall not answer them.
22.43:
“And I beat them as dust of the earth, 
I beat them small as dirt in the streets - 
I spread them out.
22.45:
“Sons of the foreigner submit to me, 
As soon as they hear they obey me.
22.46:
“Sons of the foreigner fade away, 
And gird themselves from their strongholds.
22.47:
“𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives! And baruḵ is my Rock! 
And exalted is my Elohim, 
The Rock of my deliverance,
22.48:
“Ĕl who avenges me, 
And bringing peoples down under me,
22.50:
“Therefore I give thanks to You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, among nations, 
And I sing praise to Your Name.
22.51:
“A tower of deliverance is He to His meleḵ, 
And showing kindness to His anointed, 
To Dawiḏ and his seed, forever.”

23.1: And these are the last words of Dawiḏ, the saying of Dawiḏ son of Yishai, the saying of the man raised up on high, the anointed of the Elohim of Ya’aqoḇ, and the sweet singer of Yisra’ĕl:
23.2:
“The Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken through me, 
And His Word is on my tongue.
23.3:
“The Elohim of Yisra’ĕl said, 
The Rock of Yisra’ĕl spoke to me, 
‘One who rules over man righteously, 
Who rules in the reverence of Elohim,
23.4:
“Is like the light of the morning when the sun rises, 
A morning without clouds, 
Tender grass from the earth 
From sunshine, from rain.’
23.5:
“For is not my house so with Ĕl? 
For He has made an everlasting Covenant with me, 
Ordered in all, and guarded. 
For all my deliverance and all desire, 
Shall He not make it send forth a Branch?
23.6:
“But the worthless are all as thorns thrust away, 
For they are not taken with hands,
23.7:
“But the man who touches them 
Uses iron or the shaft of a spear, 
And with fire they are burned up in place.”
23.8: These are the names of the mighty men whom Dawiḏ had: Yoshĕḇ Bashsheḇeth the Taḥkemonite, chief among the officers, he was Aḏino the Etsnite, for eight hundred slain at one time.
23.9: And after him was El’azar son of Doḏo, the Aḥoḥite, one of the three mighty men with Dawiḏ when they taunted the Pelishtites who were gathered there for battle, and the men of Yisra’ĕl had gone up.
23.10: He arose and smote the Pelishtites until his hand was weary, but his hand clung to the sword, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brought about a great deliverance that day. And the people returned after him only to plunder.
23.11: And after him was Shammah son of Aḡĕ the Hararite. And the Pelishtites had gathered into a company where there was a plot of ground covered with lentils, and the people fled from the Pelishtites.
23.12: But he took his stand in the middle of the field, and delivered it, and smote the Pelishtites, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 wrought a great deliverance.
23.13: And three of the thirty chief men went down at harvest time and came to Dawiḏ at the cave of Aḏullam, while the army of Pelishtites encamped in the Valley of Repha’im.
23.14: And Dawiḏ was then in the stronghold, while a watch-post of the Pelishtites was then in Bĕyth Leḥem.
23.15: And Dawiḏ longed and said, “Oh that someone would give me a drink of the water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem, which is by the gate!”
23.16: And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Pelishtites, and drew water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to Dawiḏ. But he would not drink it, but poured it out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.17: And he said, “Far be it from me, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to do this - the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives!” So he would not drink it. This is what the three mighty men did.
23.18: And Aḇishai the brother of Yo’aḇ, son of Tseruyah, was chief of another three. And he lifted his spear against three hundred men whom he slew, and had a name among these three.
23.19: Was he not the most esteemed of three? And he became their commander, but he did not come to the first three.
23.20: And Benayahu was the son of Yahoyaḏa, son of a brave man from Qaḇtse’ĕl, great in deeds. He smote two lion-like men of Mo’aḇ. And he went down and smote a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.
23.21: And he smote a Mitsrite, an impressive man. And the Mitsrite had a spear in his hand, so he went down to him with a staff, wrenched the spear out of the Mitsrite’s hand, and slew him with, his own spear.
23.22: This is what Benayahu son of Yahoyaḏa did, and had a name among three mighty men.
23.23: He was more esteemed than the thirty, but he did not come to the first three. And Dawiḏ put him over his guard.
23.24: Asah’ĕl the brother of Yo’aḇ was one of the thirty; Elḥanan son of Doḏo of Bĕyth Leḥem,
23.25: Shammah the Ḥaroḏite, Eliqa the Ḥaroḏite,
23.26: Ḥelets the Paltite, Ira son of Iqqĕsh the Teqowite,
23.27: Aḇi’ezer the Anethothite, Meḇunnai the Ḥushathite,
23.28: Tsalmon the Aḥoḥite, Maharai the Netophathite,
23.29: Ḥĕleḇ son of Ba’anah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Riḇai from Giḇ’ah of the children of Binyamin,
23.30: Benayahu the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the wadis of Ga’ash,
23.31: Aḇi-Alḇon the Arbathite, Azmaweth the Barḥumite,
23.32: Elyaḥba the Sha’albonite of the sons of Yashĕn, Yahonathan,
23.33: Shammah the Hararite, Aḥyam son of Sharar the Hararite,
23.34: Eliphelet son of Aḥasbai, son of the Ma’aḵathite, Eliyam son of Aḥithophel the Gilonite,
23.35: Ḥetsrai the Karmelite, Pa’arai the Arbite,
23.36: Yiḡ’al son of Nathan of Tsoḇah, Bani the Gaḏite,
23.37: Tseleq the Ammonite, Naḥarai the Be’ĕrothite, armor-bearer of Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah,
23.38: Ira the Yithrite, Garĕḇ the Yithrite,
23.39: and Uriyah the Ḥittite - thirty-seven in all.

24.1: And again the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against Yisra’ĕl, and moved Dawiḏ against them to say, “Go, number Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah.”
24.2: And the meleḵ said to Yo’aḇ the commander of the army who was with him, “Go please, throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa, and register the people, so that I know the number of the people.”
