24.3: And Yo’aḇ said to the meleḵ, “Even if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim adds to the people a hundredfold more than there are, and the eyes of my master the meleḵ see it, but why does my master the meleḵ delight in this matter?”
24.4: However, the meleḵ’s word prevailed against Yo’aḇ and against the commanders of the army. And Yo’aḇ and the commanders of the army went out from the presence of the meleḵ to register the people of Yisra’ĕl.
24.5: And they passed over the Yardĕn and camped in Aro’ĕr, on the right side of the town which is in the midst of the wadi of Gaḏ, and toward Ya’zĕr.
24.6: Then they came to Gil’aḏ and to the land of Taḥtim Ḥoḏshi, and they came to Dan Ya’an and around to Tsiḏon.
24.7: And they came to the stronghold of Tsor and to all the cities of the Ḥiwwites and the Kena’anites, and went out to South Yahuḏah as far as Be’ĕrsheḇa.
24.8: And when they had gone through all the land, they came to Yerushalayim at the end of nine months and twenty days.
24.9: And Yo’aḇ gave the number of the registration of the people to the meleḵ, and there were in Yisra’ĕl eight hundred thousand brave men who drew the sword, and the men of Yahuḏah were five hundred thousand men.
24.10: And the heart of Dawiḏ smote him after he had numbered the people. And Dawiḏ said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “l have sinned greatly in what I have done. But now, I pray, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, take away the wickedness of Your servant, for I have done very foolishly.”
24.11: And Dawiḏ rose up in the morning, and the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to the naḇi Gaḏ, Dawiḏ’s seer, saying,
24.12: “Go, and you shall speak to Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I hold three before you. Choose one of them, and I do it to you.” ’ ”
24.13: Gaḏ then came to Dawiḏ and informed him. And he said to him, “Should seven years of scarcity of food come to you in your land? Or would you flee three months before your enemies, while they pursue you? Or should there be three days’ plague in your land? Now know and see what answer I take back to Him who sent me.”
24.14: And Dawiḏ said to Gaḏ, “I am in great trouble. Please let us fall into the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for His compassion is great, but do not let me fall into the hand of man.”
24.15: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent a plague upon Yisra’ĕl from the morning till the appointed time, and from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa seventy thousand men of the people died.
24.16: And the messenger stretched out His hand over Yerushalayim to destroy it, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 relented concerning the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying the people, “It is enough, now stop Your hand.” And the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was by the threshing-floor of Arawnah the Yeḇusite.
24.17: And Dawiḏ spoke to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 when he saw the messenger who was smiting the people, and said, “See, I have sinned, and I have done perversely. But these sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father’s house.”
24.18: And Gaḏ came that day to Dawiḏ and said to him, “Go up, raise an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the threshing-floor of Arawnah the Yeḇusite.”
24.19: And Dawiḏ, according to the word of Gaḏ, went up as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded.
24.20: And Arawnah looked and saw the meleḵ and his servants coming toward him. And Arawnah went out and bowed before the meleḵ with his face to the ground.
24.21: And Arawnah said, “Why has my master the meleḵ come to his servant?” And Dawiḏ said, “To buy the threshing-floor from you, to build an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, so that the plague be withdrawn from the people.”
24.22: And Arawnah said to Dawiḏ, “Let my master the meleḵ take and offer that which seems good to him. Here are cattle for burnt offering, and threshing implements and the yokes of the cattle for wood.
24.23: “All these, O meleḵ, Arawnah has given to the meleḵ.” And Arawnah said to the meleḵ, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim accept you!”
24.24: And the meleḵ said to Arawnah, “No, let me buy it from you for a price, for certain. I am not offering burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim without cost.” So Dawiḏ bought the threshing-floor and the cattle for fifty sheqels of silver.
24.25: And Dawiḏ built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 answered the prayers for the land, and the plague was withdrawn from Yisra’ĕl.

3.1: And the fighting between the house of Sha’ul and the house of Dawiḏ was long drawn out. And Dawiḏ continued to strengthen, but the house of Sha’ul continued to weaken. But he refused to turn aside,
3.2: And sons were born to Dawiḏ in Ḥeḇron. And his first-born was Amnon by Aḥino’am the Yizre’ĕlitess;
3.3: and his second, Kil’aḇ, by Aḇiḡayil the widow of Naḇal the Karmelite; and the third, Aḇshalom son of Ma’aḵah, the daughter of Talmai, meleḵ of Geshur;
3.4: and the fourth, Aḏoniyah son of Ḥaggith; and the fifth, Shephatyah son of Aḇital;
3.5: and the sixth, Yithre’am, by Dawiḏ’s wife Eḡlah. These were born to Dawiḏ in Ḥeḇron.
3.6: And it came to be, while there was fighting between the house of Sha’ul and the house of Dawiḏ, that Aḇnĕr was strengthening himself in the house of Sha’ul.
3.7: And Sha’ul had a concubine, whose name was Ritspah, daughter of Ayah. And Ishbosheth said to Aḇnĕr, “Why have you gone in to my father’s concubine?”
3.8: And Aḇnĕr was very displeased at the words of Ishbosheth, and said, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Yahuḏah, that I show kindness to the house of Sha’ul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends today, and have not let you fall into the hand of Dawiḏ, that you charge me today with a wickedness concerning this woman?
3.9: “Elohim does so to Aḇnĕr, and more also, if I do not do for Dawiḏ as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sworn to him:
3.10: to cause the reign to pass over from the house of Sha’ul, and to raise up the throne of Dawiḏ over Yisra’ĕl and over Yahuḏah, from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa.”
3.11: And he was unable to answer Aḇnĕr another word, because he feared him.
3.12: And Aḇnĕr sent messengers on his behalf to Dawiḏ, saying, “Whose is the land?” saying also, “Make your covenant with me, and see, my hand is with you to bring all Yisra’ĕl to you.”
3.13: And Dawiḏ said, “Good, I make a covenant with you. Only one matter I am asking of you: you do not see my face unless you first bring Miḵal, daughter of Sha’ul, when you come to see my face.”
3.14: Dawiḏ then sent messengers to Ishbosheth son of Sha’ul, saying, “Give me my wife Miḵal, to whom I became engaged for a hundred foreskins of the Pelishtites.”
3.15: And Ishbosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Palti’ĕl son of Layish.
3.16: But her husband went with her to Baḥurim, going on and weeping behind her. And Aḇnĕr said to him, “Go, turn back!” And he turned back.
3.17: And Aḇnĕr had a word with the elders of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “In time past you were seeking for Dawiḏ to be meleḵ over you.
3.18: “And now, do it! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken of Dawiḏ, saying, ‘By the hand of My servant Dawiḏ, I save My people Yisra’ĕl from the hand of the Pelishtites and the hand of all their enemies.’ ”
3.19: And Aḇnĕr also spoke in the hearing of Binyamin. And Aḇnĕr also went to speak in the hearing of Dawiḏ in Ḥeḇron all that seemed good to Yisra’ĕl and all the house of Binyamin.
3.20: And Aḇnĕr and twenty men with him came to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron. And Dawiḏ made a feast for Aḇnĕr and the men who were with him.
3.21: And Aḇnĕr said to Dawiḏ, “Let me arise and go, and gather all Yisra’ĕl to my master the meleḵ, and let them make a covenant with you, and you shall reign over all that your being desires.” And Dawiḏ sent Aḇnĕr away, and he went in peace.
3.22: And see, the servants of Dawiḏ and Yo’aḇ came from a raid and brought much spoil with them. But Aḇnĕr was not with Dawiḏ in Ḥeḇron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
3.23: And Yo’aḇ and all the army that was with him came, and they reported to Yo’aḇ, saying, “Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr came to the meleḵ, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace.”
3.24: And Yo’aḇ went to the meleḵ and said, “What have you done? See, Aḇnĕr has come to you! Why is it that you sent him away, and he has already gone?
3.25: “You know that Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr came to deceive you, to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing.”
3.26: Yo’aḇ then left Dawiḏ, and he sent messengers after Aḇnĕr, who brought him back from the well of Sirah. But Dawiḏ did not know it.
3.27: Thus Aḇnĕr returned to Ḥeḇron, and Yo’aḇ took him aside in the gate to speak with him privately, and there struck him in the stomach, so that he died for the blood of Asah’ĕl his brother.
3.28: And when Dawiḏ heard it afterwards, he said, “My reign and I are guiltless before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 forever of the blood of Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr.
3.29: “Let it rest on the head of Yo’aḇ and on all his father’s house. And let there never fail to be in the house of Yo’aḇ one who has a discharge or is a leper, who leans on a staff or falls by the sword, or who lacks bread.”
3.30: So Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai his brother slew Aḇnĕr, because he had killed their brother Asah’ĕl at Giḇ’on in the battle.
3.31: And Dawiḏ said to Yo’aḇ and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your garments, gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn for Aḇnĕr.” And Meleḵ Dawiḏ followed the coffin.
3.32: And they buried Aḇnĕr in Ḥeḇron. And the meleḵ lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Aḇnĕr, and all the people wept.
3.33: And the meleḵ sang a lament over Aḇnĕr and said, “Should Aḇnĕr die as a fool dies?
3.34: “Your hands were not bound nor your feet put into shackles. As one falls before sons of evil, so you fell.” And all the people wept over him again.
3.35: And all the people came to cause Dawiḏ to eat food while it was still day, but Dawiḏ swore, saying, “Elohim do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread or whatever else till the sun goes down!”
3.36: And all the people took note of it, and it was good in their eyes, since whatever the meleḵ did was good in the eyes of all the people.
3.37: And all the people and all Yisra’ĕl knew that day that it had not been the meleḵ’s intent to kill Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr.
3.38: The meleḵ also said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great one has fallen in Yisra’ĕl today?
3.39: “And I am weak today, though anointed meleḵ. And these men, the sons of Tseruyah, are too harsh for me. Let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 repay the evil-doer according to his evil.”

4.1: And the son of Sha’ul heard that Aḇnĕr had died in Ḥeḇron, and he lost heart, and all Yisra’ĕl was troubled.
4.2: And the son of Sha’ul had two men, commanders of bands, and the name of one was Ba’anah and the name of the other Rĕḵaḇ, sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, of the children of Binyamin. For Be’ĕroth was also reckoned to Binyamin,
4.3: because the Be’ĕrothites fled to Gittayim and have been sojourners there until this day.
4.4: Now Yahonathan, son of Sha’ul, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news about Sha’ul and Yahonathan came from Yizre’ĕl, and his nurse took him up and fled. And it came to be, as she hurried to flee, that he fell and became lame. And his name was Mephiḇosheth.
4.5: So the sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, Rĕḵaḇ and Ba’anah, went and came at about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who was lying on his bed at noon.
4.6: And they came into the midst of the house, to fetch wheat, and they struck him in the stomach, and Rĕḵaḇ and Ba’anah his brother escaped.
4.7: Thus they came into the house when he was lying on his bed in his bedroom, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him. And they took his head, and went the way of the desert plain all night,
4.8: and brought the head of Ishbosheth to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron, and said to the meleḵ, “See, the head of Ishbosheth, the son of Sha’ul your enemy, who sought your life. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given my master the meleḵ vengeance on Sha’ul and his seed this day.”
4.9: And Dawiḏ answered Rĕḵaḇ and Ba’anah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, and said to them, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, who has redeemed my life out of all distress,
4.10: when someone reported to me, saying, ‘See, Sha’ul is dead,’ and he was a bearer of good news in his own eyes, I then took hold of him and slew him in Tsiqlaḡ, which was the reward I gave him for his news.
4.11: “How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous man in his own house on his bed, should I not now require his blood at your hand and remove you from the earth?”
4.12: And Dawiḏ commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and feet, and hanged them by the pool in Ḥeḇron. And they took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the tomb of Aḇnĕr in Ḥeḇron.

5.1: And all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl came to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron and spoke, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.
5.2: “Formerly, when Sha’ul was meleḵ over us, you were the one who led Yisra’ĕl out and brought them in. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to you, ‘Shepherd My people Yisra’ĕl, and be ruler over Yisra’ĕl.’ ”
5.3: And all the elders of Yisra’ĕl came to the meleḵ at Ḥeḇron, and Meleḵ Dawiḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they anointed Dawiḏ meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl.
5.4: Dawiḏ was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
5.5: In Ḥeḇron he reigned over Yahuḏah seven years and six months, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years over all Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah.
5.6: And the meleḵ and his men went to Yerushalayim against the Yeḇusites, the inhabitants of the land. And they spoke to Dawiḏ, saying, “Except you take away the blind and the lame, you are not going to come in here,” thinking, “Dawiḏ is not going to come in here.”
5.7: But Dawiḏ captured the stronghold of Tsiyon, the City of Dawiḏ.
5.8: And Dawiḏ said on that day, “Anyone who reaches the water-shaft, let him smite the Yeḇusites and the lame and the blind, who are hated by Dawiḏ’s being.” That is why they say, “The blind and the lame do not come into the house.”
5.9: And Dawiḏ dwelt in the stronghold, and called it the City of Dawiḏ. And Dawiḏ built all around from ha’Millo and inward.
5.10: And Dawiḏ went on and became great, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of hosts was with him.
5.11: Now Ḥiram meleḵ of Tsor sent messengers to Dawiḏ, and cedar trees, and carpenters and masons. And they built a house for Dawiḏ.
5.12: And Dawiḏ knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had established him as meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl, and that He had exalted His reign, because of His people Yisra’ĕl.
5.13: And Dawiḏ took more concubines and wives from Yerushalayim, after he had come from Ḥeḇron, and more sons and daughters were born to Dawiḏ.
5.14: And these were the names of those born to him in Yerushalayim: Shammua, and Shoḇaḇ, and Nathan, and Shelomoh,
5.15: and Yiḇḥar, and Elishua, Nepheḡ, and Yaphiya,
5.16: and Elishama, and Elyaḏa, and Eliphelet.
5.17: And the Pelishtites heard that they had anointed Dawiḏ meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl, and all the Pelishtites went up to search for Dawiḏ, but Dawiḏ heard and went down to the stronghold.
5.18: And the Pelishtites came and spread themselves out in the Valley of Repha’im.
5.19: And Dawiḏ inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “Do I go up against the Pelishtites? Do You give them into my hand?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Dawiḏ, “Go up, for I shall certainly give the Pelishtites into your hand.”
5.20: And Dawiḏ came to Ba’al Peratsim, and Dawiḏ smote them there. And he said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has broken through my enemies before me, like a breakthrough of water.” So he called the name of that place Ba’al Peratsim.
5.21: And they left their images there, and Dawiḏ and his men took them away.
5.22: And the Pelishtites again came up and were spread out in the Valley of Repha’im.
5.23: And when Dawiḏ inquired of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, He said, “Do not go up, turn around behind them, and you shall come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.
5.24: “And it shall be, when you hear the sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then act promptly, for then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall go out before you to smite the camp of the Pelishtites.”
5.25: And Dawiḏ did so, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded him, and smote the Pelishtites from Geḇa as far as Gezer.

6.1: Now Dawiḏ again gathered all the chosen men of Yisra’ĕl, thirty thousand.
6.2: And Dawiḏ rose up and went with all the people who were with him from Ba’alĕ Yahuḏah, to bring up from there the ark of Elohim, that is called by the Name, the Name 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Hosts, who dwells between the keruḇim.
6.3: And they placed the ark of Elohim on a new wagon, and brought it from the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, which was on the hill. And Uzzah and Aḥyo, sons of Aḇinaḏaḇ, were leading the new wagon.
6.4: And they brought it from the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, which was on the hill, with the ark of Elohim. And Aḥyo was walking before the ark.
6.5: And Dawiḏ and all the house of Yisra’ĕl were dancing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, with all fir wood instruments, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with sistrums, and with cymbals.
6.6: And when they came to the threshing-floor of Naḵon, Uzzah reached out toward the ark of Elohim and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.
6.7: And the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against Uzzah, and Elohim smote him there for the fault. And he died there by the ark of Elohim.
6.8: And Dawiḏ was displeased because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had broken out against Uzzah. And he called the name of the place Perets Uzzah, until this day.
6.9: And Dawiḏ was afraid of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on that day, and said, “How shall the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 come to me?”
6.10: And Dawiḏ would not move the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with him into the City of Dawiḏ, but Dawiḏ turned it aside to the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom the Gittite.
6.11: And the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 remained in the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom the Gittite three months, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 baraḵ Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and all his house.
6.12: And it was reported to Meleḵ Dawiḏ, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has baraḵ the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and all that he has, because of the ark of Elohim.” Dawiḏ then went and brought up the ark of Elohim from the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom to the City of Dawiḏ with rejoicing.
6.13: And it came to be, when those bearing the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had gone six steps, that he slaughtered bulls and fatlings.
6.14: And Dawiḏ danced before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all his might. And Dawiḏ was wearing a linen shoulder garment.
6.15: Thus Dawiḏ and all the house of Yisra’ĕl brought up the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with shouting and with the sound of the ram’s horn.
6.16: And it came to be, when the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came into the City of Dawiḏ, that Miḵal, daughter of Sha’ul, looked through a window and saw Meleḵ Dawiḏ leaping and dancing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and she despised him in her heart.
6.17: So they brought the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in, and put it in its place in the midst of the Tent that Dawiḏ had pitched for it. And Dawiḏ brought burnt offerings before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and peace offerings.
6.18: And when Dawiḏ had finished bringing burnt offerings and peace offerings, he baraḵ the people in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts.
6.19: And he apportioned to all the people, to all the crowd of Yisra’ĕl, from man even to women, to each one a loaf of bread, and a measure, and a cake of raisins. And all the people left, each one to his house.
6.20: And Dawiḏ returned to baraḵ his household, and Miḵal the daughter of Sha’ul came out to meet Dawiḏ, and said, “How esteemed was the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl today, uncovering himself today in the eyes of the female servants of his servants, as one of the foolish ones shamelessly uncovers himself!”
6.21: So Dawiḏ said to Miḵal, “Before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who chose me instead of your father and all his house, commanding me to be ruler over the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, over Yisra’ĕl, so I danced before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
6.22: “And I shall be even more slight than this, and shall be humble in my own eyes. But as for the female servants of whom you have spoken, by them I am esteemed.”
6.23: And Miḵal the daughter of Sha’ul had no children to the day of her death.

7.1: And it came to be when the meleḵ was dwelling in his house, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had given him rest from all his enemies all around,
7.2: that the meleḵ said to Nathan the naḇi, “See now, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, but the ark of Elohim dwells within curtains.”
7.3: And Nathan said to the meleḵ, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with you.”
7.4: And it came to be that night that the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Nathan, saying,
7.5: “Go and say to My servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Would you build a house for Me to dwell in?
7.6: “For I have not dwelt in a house since the time that I brought the children of Yisra’ĕl up from Mitsrayim, even to this day, but have moved about in a Tent and in a Dwelling Place.
7.7: “Wherever I have walked with all the children of Yisra’ĕl, have I ever spoken a word to anyone from the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?’ ” ’
7.8: “And now, say to My servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over My people, over Yisra’ĕl.
7.9: “And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you, and have made you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
7.10: “And I shall appoint a place for My people Yisra’ĕl, and shall plant them, and they shall dwell in a place of their own and no longer be afraid, neither shall the children of wickedness oppress them again, as at the first,
7.11: even from the day I appointed rulers over My people Yisra’ĕl, and have caused you to rest from all your enemies. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has declared to you that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would make you a house.
7.12: “When your days are filled and you rest with your fathers, I shall raise up your seed after you, who comes from your inward parts, and shall establish his reign.
7.13: “He builds a house for My Name, and I shall establish the throne of his reign forever.
7.14: “I am to be his Father, and he is My son. If he does perversely, I shall reprove him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.
7.15: “But My kindness does not turn aside from him, as I turned it aside from Sha’ul, whom I removed from before you.
7.16: “And your house and your reign are to be steadfast forever before you - your throne is established forever.” ’ ”
7.17: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to Dawiḏ.
7.18: And Meleḵ Dawiḏ went in and sat before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and he said, “Who am I, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄? And what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
7.19: “And yet this was a small matter in Your eyes, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And You have also spoken of Your servant’s house for a great while to come. And is this the teaching of man, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
7.20: “And what more does Dawiḏ say to You? For You, Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, know Your servant.
7.21: “Because of Your word, and according to Your own heart, You have done all this greatness, to make it known to Your servant.
7.22: “You are great indeed, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. For there is none like You, and there is no Elohim but You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
7.23: “And who is like Your people, like Yisra’ĕl, the one nation on the earth whom Elohim went to redeem for Himself as a people, to make for Himself a Name, and to do for You greatness, and awesome deeds for Your land before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Mitsrayim, from the nations and their mighty ones?
7.24: “And You have established for Yourself Your people Yisra’ĕl as Your own people forever, and You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, have become their Elohim.
7.25: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, the word which You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house, establish it forever and do as You have said.
7.26: “And let Your Name be made great forever, saying, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts is the Elohim over Yisra’ĕl.’ And let the house of Your servant Dawiḏ be established before You.
7.27: “For You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, have revealed this to Your servant, saying, ‘I build you a house.’ Therefore Your servant has taken heart to pray this prayer to You.
7.28: “And now, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You are Elohim, and Your words are true, and You have spoken this goodness to Your servant.
7.29: “And now, be pleased to baraḵ the house of Your servant, to be before You, forever. For You, O Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, have spoken it, and with Your beraḵah may the house of Your servant receive beraḵah forever.”

8.1: And after this it came to be that Dawiḏ smote the Pelishtites and humbled them. And Dawiḏ took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Pelishtites.
8.2: He also smote Mo’aḇ, and measured them off with a line, causing them to lie down on the earth. With two lines he measured off those to be put to death, and with one complete line those to be kept alive. And the Mo’aḇites became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents.
8.3: Dawiḏ also smote Haḏaḏezer son of Reḥoḇ, meleḵ of Tsoḇah, as he went to restore his rule at the River Perath.
8.4: And Dawiḏ captured from him one thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Dawiḏ destroyed all the chariots, but he left of them a hundred chariots.
8.5: And the Arameans of Dammeseq came to help Haḏaḏezer meleḵ of Tsoḇah, and Dawiḏ smote twenty-two thousand of the Arameans.
8.6: Then Dawiḏ put watch-posts in Aram of Dammeseq. And the Arameans became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved Dawiḏ wherever he went.
8.7: And Dawiḏ took the shields of gold which were on the servants of Haḏaḏezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim.
8.8: And from Betaḥ and from Bĕrothai, cities of Haḏaḏezer, Meleḵ Dawiḏ took very much bronze.
8.9: And To’i meleḵ of Ḥamath heard that Dawiḏ had smitten all the army of Haḏaḏezer,
8.10: so To’i sent Yoram his son to Meleḵ Dawiḏ, to ask peace of him and baraḵ him, because he had fought against Haḏaḏezer and smote him, for Haḏaḏezer had battles with To’i. And brought with him objects of silver, and objects of gold, and objects of bronze.
8.11: Meleḵ Dawiḏ also qadosh these to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, along with the silver and gold that he had qadosh from all the nations which he had humbled:
8.12: from Aram, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Pelishtites, and from Amalĕq, and from the spoil of Haḏaḏezer son of Reḥoḇ, meleḵ of Tsoḇah.
8.13: And Dawiḏ made a name when he returned from smiting eighteen thousand Arameans in the Valley of Salt.
8.14: And he put watch-posts in Eḏom. Throughout all Eḏom he put watch-posts, and all the Eḏomites became Dawiḏ’s servants. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved Dawiḏ wherever he went.
8.15: And Dawiḏ reigned over all Yisra’ĕl, and Dawiḏ was doing right-ruling and righteousness to all his people.
8.16: And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah was over the army, and Yahoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder,
8.17: and Tsaḏoq son of Aḥituḇ and Aḥimeleḵ son of Eḇyathar were the kohenim, and Serayah was the scribe,
8.18: and Benayahu son of Yahoyaḏa was over both the Kerĕthites and the Pelĕthites, and Dawiḏ’s sons were kohenim.

9.1: And Dawiḏ said, “Is there still anyone who is left of the house of Sha’ul, that I might show him kindness, because of Yahonathan?”
9.2: And the house of Sha’ul had a servant whose name was Tsiḇa. And they had called him to Dawiḏ, and the meleḵ said to him, “Are you Tsiḇa?” And he said, “Your servant!”
9.3: And the meleḵ said, “Is there not still someone of the house of Sha’ul, so that I show him the kindness of Elohim?” And Tsiḇa said to the meleḵ, “There is still a son of Yahonathan, lame in his feet.”
9.4: So the meleḵ said to him, “Where is he?” And Tsiḇa said to the meleḵ, “See, he is in the house of Maḵir son of Ammi’ĕl, in Lo Ḏeḇar.”
9.5: And Meleḵ Dawiḏ sent and brought him out of the house of Maḵir son of Ammi’ĕl, from Lo Ḏeḇar.
9.6: And Mephiḇosheth son of Yahonathan, son of Sha’ul, came to Dawiḏ, and fell on his face and did obeisance. And Dawiḏ said, “Mephiḇosheth!” And he answered, “Here is your servant!”
9.7: Dawiḏ then said to him, “Do not fear, for I shall certainly show you kindness because of Yahonathan your father, and shall return to you all the land of Sha’ul your grandfather, and let you eat bread at my table continually.”
9.8: And he bowed himself and said, “What is your servant, that you should turn to such a dead dog as I?”
9.9: And the meleḵ called Tsiḇa servant of Sha’ul, and said to him, “I have given to your master’s son all that belonged to Sha’ul and to all his house.
9.10: “And you and your sons and your servants, shall work the land for him, and you shall bring, and your master’s son shall have food to eat. But let Mephiḇosheth your master’s son eat bread at my table always.” And Tsiḇa had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
9.11: And Tsiḇa said to the meleḵ, “According to all that my master the meleḵ has commanded his servant, so your servant does.” “As for Mephiḇosheth, he shall eat at my table as one of the sons of the meleḵ.”
9.12: And Mephiḇosheth had a young son whose name was Miḵa. And all who dwelt in the house of Tsiḇa were servants of Mephiḇosheth.
9.13: And Mephiḇosheth was dwelling in Yerushalayim, for he ate continually at the meleḵ’s table. And he was lame in both his feet.
